video.title: Dynasty Fantasy Basketball Rookie Ranks For The 2026 NBA Draft Class - Part 1

summary: Josh Lloyd ranks the 2026 NBA draft class for dynasty leagues in part 1 of 2. This part covers tiers 14 through 4, which is ranks 94 to 13, and the top 12 come in a later show. The rankings mostly target category leagues and combine age, talent, fantasy skill and draft capital. He says leagues that keep only a few players should ignore everyone except the top two or three rookies. He also says dynasty leagues should be at least 300 players deep and should hold a separate rookie-only draft. His main takes: he is low on Alex Karaban and the Warriors' number 11 pick, he likes Cleveland's Malik Thomas pick and Labaron Philon, and he is high on late picks Onu Yensu and Henri Veesaar. Many names in the auto captions are garbled. Where the real name could not be worked out with confidence, the note says so.

rules.text: If your dynasty league keeps only about three players, prioritize only the top two to three rookies and almost no others.
rules.quote: If your league keeps three players, you should not realistically be prioritizing nearly any rookie apart from the top two to three guys

rules.text: Dynasty leagues should be at least 300 players deep.
rules.quote: Dynasty leagues should be 300 deep minimum.

rules.text: Dynasty leagues should run a separate draft for rookies only, not for cut players or existing free agents.
rules.quote: should have a separate draft for rookies. Not players that get cut, not existing NBA free agents, rookies only.

rules.text: The rookie ranking formula combines age, talent, fantasy skill and draft capital invested.
rules.quote: taking age, talent, fantasy skill, draft capital invested to create a ranking formula

rules.text: Adjust rookie rankings to your league position. Contenders want players who help in years one and two. Rebuilders can wait for players who break out in years four or five.
rules.quote: They'll bump up in years four to five. And depending on where you sit in your dynasty league, you have to make those adjustments.

rules.text: Players in the same tier are close in value and can be swapped for each other.
rules.quote: Anyone that's in a tier, I find them to be pretty close to each other.

rules.text: Contract status changes a lot right after the draft. Exhibit 10 deals can become two-way deals, so check before you draft.
rules.quote: Some of these players that are on exhibit 10s can be turned into two-ways.

rules.text: Draft-and-stash overseas players lose value because some of them never come over to the NBA.
rules.quote: cuz if you don't come over, there's a chance he never comes over.

rules.text: A 24-year-old rookie should ideally be starting and producing right away. Older rookies have less upside.
rules.quote: At 24, you generally would want your rookies to be starting and starting to really do stuff.

rules.text: Draft capital counts in the rankings, but he trusts it less when it comes from a team he doubts, like the Bucks.
rules.quote: But draft capital was invested. All right, put less faith in that because it's the Bucks.
